elements.element: On expiry or termination, Vendor must provide transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 expressly requires Vendor to provide transition assistance on expiry or termination.

elements.element: Transition assistance must be available for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 specifies assistance “for up to six months.”

elements.element: Transition assistance must be provided at Vendor's then-current rates.
On expiry or termination, Vendor must return Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 imposes an unconditional return obligation on expiry or termination.

elements.element: Customer Data must be returned within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 requires return within thirty days, and its opening trigger is expiry or termination.

elements.element: Customer Data must be returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Section 11.2 specifies a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, but that obligation is triggered only by Customer's request. The unconditional post-termination return obligation in Section 11.1 does not itself specify the required format.

elements.element: After return of Customer Data, Vendor must certify its deletion.
elements.evidence: Section 11.3 requires written certification by an authorized officer, but only after Customer confirms successful return. Because Customer confirmation is an additional condition that may never occur, certification is not unconditionally required after return as contemplated by the preferred position.

elements.element: On expiry or termination, Vendor must provide transition assistance for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 makes transition assistance available for up to six months, which encompasses the fallback 90-day period.

elements.element: On expiry or termination, Vendor must export Customer Data within 30 days.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 requires Vendor to return Customer Data within thirty days after expiry or termination; this satisfies the fallback data-export requirement.

result.reason: The redline surgically removes the walk-away provision and fully achieves the fallback. It does not fully achieve the preferred position because the machine-readable-format duty remains conditioned on a Customer request, and deletion certification remains conditioned on Customer confirmation of successful return. Sections 11.1 and 11.2 also create overlapping return obligations with different triggers, reducing clarity, although unrelated commercial terms remain effective and no direct contradiction is introduced.
